text: Make each check a connect-the-dots picture: source promise → visible consequence → independent acceptance question.
rationale: A missing dot exposes a guidance gap; a broken dot exposes execution error without adding a second validation ritual.

text: Treat exact words like toy blocks: match them only when the source says the block’s shape matters; otherwise match the behavior built from them.
rationale: This separates contract-critical wording and model strings from brittle descriptive assertions without waiving substantive checks.

text: For every JSON check, ask the document a real path question and print the path with its answer before deciding true or false.
rationale: The output makes Path-versus-string mistakes immediately visible while preserving the actual value check.

text: When a checker fails, make it point to the first broken arrow—source, behavior, or report—instead of launching a new checker.
rationale: The next action becomes evidence-led repair, not an arbitrary retry or duplicate script.

text: Read the changed source and final report as one comic strip, then have acceptance read a different strip without borrowing its ending.
rationale: One inspection covers pointer/report coherence while acceptance stays independent and unchanged-product packaging work disappears.

text: Ask the worker to say “because” twice: the claim is true because the source says X, and the result is real because observation Y happened.
rationale: Two concrete reasons expose unsupported prose early while retaining source proof, behavioral proof, and final acceptance.
